originalTitle: Councils to share £5m in 'emergency food aid' as living costs rise
summary: The money from the Welsh government will amount to around £200,000 to every council.
content:
Deputy First Minister Sioned Williams says families are facing a "tough winter" with inflation rising

Welsh councils will receive £4.8 million to provide "emergency food aid" and other support for people struggling due to cost of living pressures.

The cash from the Welsh government will be split between the 22 local authorities, with those in rural areas getting a premium due to "the added challenges" of delivering support to more sparsely populated regions.

Deputy First Minister Sioned Williams said rising fuel and energy costs meant many families faced another "tough winter" and she was "targeting support where it's needed most".

Reform UK Wales said the Welsh government would have more money to spend on supporting people in need if they did not "waste money" on international spending.

The ongoing US-Iran war and pressures on oil supply in Saudi Arabia have caused fuel prices to spike in recent days.

With inflation increasing and energy bills going up next month , many people could feel more of a squeeze on their household budgets.

Local authorities will be able to give the emergency money to community organisations like food banks, lunch clubs and advice providers.

Gareth Banks volunteers at Down to Zero, which grows organic vegetables for the local community

Down To Zero, a project which has received funding previously, grows vegetables on allotments near Llantrisant in Rhondda Cynon Taf, and provides free vegetable boxes to low income families as well as lower cost subscriptions to other households within the county.

Gareth Banks has volunteered with the organisation for two years and "absolutely loves it".

"We can offer really good value, organically grown, fruit and vegetables to local people who might not always be able to afford that kind of thing," he said.

Angharad Rogers says families with incomes are "still not able to pay for food"

The project is run by Cynon Taf, a social housing provider.

Angharad Rogers, Cynon Taf's director of housing and communities, said food poverty was a growing problem for tenants.

"We've seen quite a shift lately in the people... who are most in need and accessing food banks," she said.

"Families with incomes coming into the household are still not able pay for food and things like that, so we're seeing a lot families coming to us and asking for help."

Where to get help if you are struggling with bills

Contact advicelink Cymru , external for free, impartial advice on debt and benefits

Contact your local council to see if you are eligible for emergency help from the Discretionary Assistance Fund , external

If you are on a prepayment meter and cannot afford fuel you can contact the Fuel Bank Foundation , external for help

If you are on a low income, you may be able to get your council tax reduced via the council tax reduction scheme , external

Joy says fuel prices are "extraordinarily high"

UK inflation hit its highest level in five months in the year to August, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

Overall, motor fuel prices rose by 23% compared to August last year.

In Ystradowen, Vale of Glamorgan, drivers filling up their cars said they feared prices would increase further.

Ron Jones, from Cowbridge, said he was driving less but higher prices were "to be expected, given the world as it is".

Joy Thomas said prices were "extraordinarily high" and she had searched for the cheapest petrol station she could find.

Lewis Wall, 28, from Ystradowen, said prices were "ridiculous".

"But what can we do about it? You can't control the price and everyone needs fuel."

Williams said the government would "do all we can to support families who are going to be finding it tough this winter".

"But we need to see wider measures and many of those leavers reside in Westminster," she added.

She called on the UK government to bring in a system of cheaper energy prices for low income households, known as social tariffs.

"Social tariffs on energy is one of the main things I think that could really make a difference to people," she said.

The UK government said: "We have cut VAT on electricity bills from October, on top of the £150 we removed from bills earlier this year, and we will keep looking at what more we can do to protect families from unaffordable bills."

Reform said support to help ease the pressures of the cost of living "should be welcomed if delivered in the right way".

But it also said the Plaid Cymru government "could be doing more" if it did not "waste money" on projects like "spending taxpayer cash on planting trees in Uganda", referencing the long-running climate resilience program funded by it.

chineseTitle: 随着生活成本上升，各议会将分享 500 万英镑的“紧急粮食援助”
chineseSummary: 威尔士政府向每个议会提供的资金约为20万英镑。
chineseContent:
副首席部长西奥内德·威廉姆斯表示，随着通胀上升，家庭正面临“艰难的冬天”

威尔士议会将获得480万英镑，为因生活成本压力而苦苦挣扎的人们提供“紧急粮食援助”和其他支持。

威尔士政府的现金将在 22 个地方当局之间分配，农村地区的当局由于向人口稀少地区提供支持的“额外挑战”而获得溢价。

副首席部长西奥尼德·威廉姆斯表示，燃料和能源成本上涨意味着许多家庭面临另一个“艰难的冬天”，她“在最需要的地方提供支持”。

英国威尔士改革组织表示，如果威尔士政府不在国际支出上“浪费钱”，他们将有更多的钱用于支持有需要的人。

持续的美伊战争和沙特阿拉伯石油供应的压力导致近几天燃油价格飙升。

随着下个月通货膨胀的加剧和能源费用的上涨，许多人可能会感到家庭预算更加紧张。

地方当局将能够向食品银行、午餐俱乐部和咨询提供者等社区组织提供紧急资金。

加雷斯·班克斯 (Gareth Banks) 是 Down to Zero 的志愿者，该组织为当地社区种植有机蔬菜

Down To Zero 项目此前已获得资金，在 Rhondda Cynon Taf 的 Llantrisant 附近的土地上种植蔬菜，并向低收入家庭提供免费蔬菜盒，并为县内其他家庭提供较低成本的订阅。

加雷斯·班克斯 (Gareth Banks) 已在该组织担任志愿者两年，并且“非常喜欢它”。

“我们可以为当地人提供真正物有所值的有机种植的水果和蔬菜，但他们可能并不总是买得起这种东西，”他说。

安格哈拉德·罗杰斯表示，有收入的家庭“仍然无力支付食物费用”

该项目由社会住房提供商 Cynon Taf 运营。

Cynon Taf 的住房和社区主管安格哈拉德·罗杰斯 (Angharad Rogers) 表示，粮食贫困对租户来说是一个日益严重的问题。

“我们最近看到人们发生了很大的转变……他们最需要帮助并获得食物银行，”她说。

“有收入的家庭仍然无力支付食物和类似费用，所以我们看到很多家庭来找我们寻求帮助。”

联系 AdWordsLink Cymru，外部提供有关债务和福利的免费、公正的建议

请联系您当地的议会，了解您是否有资格从外部酌情援助基金获得紧急帮助

如果您使用预付费表并且买不起燃料，您可以联系外部燃料银行基金会寻求帮助

如果您的收入较低，您可以通过外部市政税减免计划来减少市政税

乔伊表示燃油价格“非常高”

英国国家统计局 (ONS) 的数据显示，截至 8 月份，英国通胀率创下 5 个月以来的最高水平。

总体而言，车用燃油价格比去年 8 月上涨了 23%。

在格拉摩根谷的伊斯特拉多文，加油的司机表示，他们担心价格会进一步上涨。

来自考布里奇的罗恩·琼斯(Ron Jones)表示，他开车的次数减少了，但价格上涨“是可以预料的，考虑到世界的现状”。

乔伊·托马斯表示，油价“非常高”，她已经寻找了她能找到的最便宜的加油站。

来自 Ystradowen 的 28 岁刘易斯·沃尔 (Lewis Wall) 表示，价格“荒谬”。

“但我们能做什么呢？你无法控制价格，每个人都需要燃料。”

威廉姆斯表示，政府将“尽我们所能来支持今年冬天生活困难的家庭”。

“但我们需要看到更广泛的措施，而且许多离开者居住在威斯敏斯特，”她补充道。

她呼吁英国政府为低收入家庭引入更便宜的能源价格体系，即社会关税。

“我认为能源社会关税是真正能够对人们产生影响的主要事情之一，”她说。

英国政府表示：“除了今年早些时候从电费账单中取消的 150 英镑增值税之外，我们从 10 月份开始还削减了电费增值税，我们将继续研究可以采取哪些措施来保护家庭免受难以负担的电费的影响。”

改革表示，有助于缓解生活成本压力的支持“如果以正确的方式提供，应该受到欢迎”。

但它还表示，如果格莱德·西姆鲁政府不“浪费金钱”在“用纳税人的钱在乌干达植树”等项目上，“可以做得更多”，并提到由其资助的长期气候适应计划。
